items.q: Acute kidney injury is defined as an abrupt decrease in renal function over hours to days resulting in:
opts: ECF volume expansion, uremia, hyperkalemia and acidosis
ECF volume depletion with hyponatremia and alkalosis
items.exp: AKI: abrupt decrease in renal function over hours to days resulting in (a) ECF volume expansion, (b) uremia, (c) hyperkalemia and (d) acidosis. (Book p796)

items.q: Fill up: The four consequences of AKI listed are ECF volume expansion, uremia, hyperkalemia and ______.
items.exp: AKI results in ECF volume expansion, uremia, hyperkalemia and acidosis. (Book p796)

items.q: Match the KDIGO stage with its urine-output criterion — 1) KDIGO 1  2) KDIGO 2  3) KDIGO 3 … A) <0.5 mL/kg/hr for ≥12 hrs  B) <0.5 mL/kg/hr for ≥6 hrs  C) <0.3 mL/kg/hr for ≥24 hrs or anuria (≤100 mL) for ≥12 hrs
items.exp: KDIGO urine-output criteria: stage 1 — <0.5 mL/kg/hr for ≥6 hrs; stage 2 — <0.5 mL/kg/hr for ≥12 hrs; stage 3 — <0.3 mL/kg/hr for ≥24 hrs or anuria (≤100 mL) for ≥12 hrs. (Book p796)

items.q: KDIGO stage 1 is met by a urine output of less than 0.5 mL/kg/hr for at least:
items.exp: KDIGO 1: urine output <0.5 mL/kg/hr for ≥6 hrs. (Book p796)

items.q: Match the KDIGO stage with its creatinine criterion — 1) KDIGO 1  2) KDIGO 2  3) KDIGO 3 … A) Raised by >2 times the baseline  B) Raised by >0.3 mg/dL or >50% in 7 days (1.5–1.9 times baseline)  C) Raised by >3 times the baseline
items.exp: KDIGO creatinine criteria: stage 1 — rise >0.3 mg/dL or >50% in 7 days (1.5–1.9 times baseline); stage 2 — >2 times baseline; stage 3 — >3 times baseline. (Book p796)

items.q: A patient's creatinine rises from 1.0 to 2.3 mg/dL over 3 days with urine output of 0.4 mL/kg/hr for 14 hours. The KDIGO stage is:
opts: KDIGO 2 — creatinine >2 times baseline and urine output <0.5 mL/kg/hr for ≥12 hrs
Not AKI — the creatinine rise is physiological
items.exp: Creatinine >2 times baseline (stage 2 creatinine) with urine output <0.5 mL/kg/hr for ≥12 hrs (stage 2 urine criterion) = KDIGO 2. (Book p796)

items.q: A man with creatinine 1.2 mg/dL develops anuria with 90 mL of urine over the last 14 hours. KDIGO stage is:
opts: AKI cannot be staged without a creatinine rise
items.exp: KDIGO 3 urine criterion: <0.3 mL/kg/hr for ≥24 hrs OR anuria (≤100 mL) for ≥12 hrs. (Book p796)

items.q: Which set lists only the newer markers of AKI given in the note?
opts: NGAL, KIM-1, cystatin C and β₂ microglobulin
KIM-1, IL-18, troponin and brain natriuretic peptide
LFABP, IL-18, C-reactive protein and procalcitonin
items.exp: Note: the newer markers in AKI are NGAL, KIM-1, LFABP and IL-18. (Book p796)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed as newer markers of AKI. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Newer AKI markers listed: NGAL, KIM-1, LFABP and IL-18. (Book p796)

items.q: In the CAUSES flowchart, the renal causes of AKI are:
opts: Acute tubular necrosis and acute interstitial nephritis
Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and HUS only
items.exp: The CAUSES flowchart divides AKI into pre-renal, renal and post-renal; the renal branch names acute tubular necrosis (ATN) and acute interstitial nephritis (AIN). (Book p796)
